correctness.rationale: For each n≥3, reduction to closed edge-covering walk is bijective by n-overlap. The graph is strongly connected by an explicit alternating connector. Every surplus source s requires at least d(s) extra edges before any deficit sink can be reached, using first-two-bit shift tracking and integral path decomposition. Complement-append paths of exactly d(s) land injectively and exhaustively in sinks because the last equal pair of an endpoint recovers its unique source. Hence Eulerian balancing matches the lower bound. Independent Fibonacci recurrence counts ∑d(s)=2F_(n−1)−2 and U_n=2F_(n+1). The n=2 case follows from four distinct required pairs and witness 0011. Both separate included source programs succeeded on their advertised finite ranges.

value.rationale: For a natural regular language defined by the smallest nontrivial symmetric run-length restriction, the factor dictionary lacks an exact-once universal cycle from n≥4 because the overlap graph is unbalanced. Determining the minimum redundancy to restore a cyclic, constraint-respecting factor-complete cover is therefore mathematically motivated. The exact Lucas count, sharp Fibonacci extra-occurrence cost, and explicit all-n Eulerian construction solve that natural minimum length for every n≥2, not an arbitrary slice or a routine special case of a known numerical table. The value lies in the sharp structural matching rather than solely in code verification; relevance is to constrained cyclic testing/sequencing and word combinatorics.
